title: Predicting Gene Silencing Through the Spatiotemporal Control of siRNA Release from Photo-responsive Polymeric Nanocarriers
protocol: Prepare separate solutions of siRNA and mPEG-b-P(APNBMA) with equal volumes in a 20 mM HEPES buffer at pH 6.0.
Add siRNA to the HEPES solution at a concentration of 32 µg/mL.
Dissolve mPEG-b-P(APNBMA) polymers into a separate 20 mM HEPES solution.
Make an appropriate amount of mPEG-b-P(APNBMA) solution to achieve a 220 µg/mL concentration in the HEPES buffer.
Add the mPEG-b-P(APNBMA) solution dropwise to the siRNA solution while gently mixing on a vortex machine.
Vortex the mixture for 30 seconds after polymer addition.
Incubate the samples in the dark at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Mix the nanocarrier with sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS).
Prepare a 1 mg/mL solution of SDS in water.
Aliquot out the amount of SDS solution needed to produce solutions with an S/P ratio of 15.
Add 13 µg of SDS to the polyplex solution containing 1 µg of siRNA to achieve an S/P ratio of 15.
Mix the SDS solution dropwise with the nanocarrier solution while gently mixing on a vortex machine.
Vortex the samples for 30 s following SDS addition.
Centrifuge the samples at 3,000 x g for 5 s.
Incubate the samples in the dark at room temperature for 30 min.
Calibrate and set a UV laser with a 365 nm filter to an intensity of 200 W/m.
Pre-wash glass slides in a 7:3 (v/v) ethanol/water solution and dry completely.
Cut a hole (~2 x 3 cm rectangle) into a rubber gasket.
Place the rubber gasket onto a glass slide.
Pipette the nanocarrier/SDS solution onto the glass slide inside the hole of the rubber gasket.
Load an excess of solution (20 µL in surplus) onto the glass slide while avoiding contact with the rubber gasket.
Place one end of the second glass slide down first and then slowly lower the other end to avoid air bubble generation.
Attach binder clips to each side of the glass chamber to hold it closed.
Irradiate the samples with a UV laser at 365 nm and an intensity of 200 W/m for the desired length of time (e.g., 0-60 min).
Remove the binder clips and open the chamber.
Pipette 25 μL of the irradiated nanocarrier/SDS samples into a microcentrifuge tube.
Incubate the solutions in the dark at room temperature for 30 min.
Prepare a 2 wt% agarose gel pre-stained with 0.5 µg/mL ethidium bromide in TBE buffered solution according to standard protocols.
Prepare a loading buffer comprised of 3:7 (v/v) glycerol/water.
Add 5 μL of the loading buffer solution to 25 μL of each nanocarrier/SDS sample.
Incubate the samples in the dark at room temperature for 10 min.
Load 30 µL of each nanocarrier/SDS sample into the 2% agarose gel.
Run the gel in the dark at 100 V for 30 min.
Image the gel using a gel imaging system with ethidium bromide filters.
Save the gel image files and proceed to step 2.10 for band intensity quantification.
Ensure that the band intensities are bright enough to clearly visualize but not too bright that the signals are saturated.
Quantify the band intensities using publicly available ImageJ software.
Using the ROI tool of ImageJ, determine the fluorescence intensity of the free siRNA bands in each lane by drawing a rectangle around each band.
Plot the intensity curves of each lane.
Integrate the area under the curves by drawing a horizontal line across the intensity curves and clicking the tracing wand inside the enclosed areas.
Compute the relative intensity of each lane by dividing the area under the curve of each sample by the area under the curve of the siRNA positive control (no mPEG-b-P(APNBMA) added and no SDS added).
Report the percentage of siRNA released as the normalized band intensity of each sample.
Obtain siRNA labelled with a single fluorophore at the 5' end of the sense strand.
Formulate the nanocarriers according to steps 1.1-1.2 using the labelled siRNA, scaling volumes as needed.
Incubate the solutions in SDS and irradiate for the desired length of time according to steps 2.2-2.6.
Wash a glass slide with a 7:3 (v/v) ethanol/water solution.
Completely dry the glass using a wipe and an air stream.
Remove pieces of paper from a double-sided adhesive spacer.
Attach the spacer to a glass coverslip.
Pipette the nanocarrier/SDS solution onto the cover slip in the middle of the hole from the adhesive spacer.
Place the glass slide on top of the coverslip.
Push on the glass slide to ensure that the glass slide and coverslip are well attached and form a seal.
Use a confocal microscope for FCS measurements.
Use a 40X water immersion apochromat objective with a numerical aperture of 1.2.
Use the appropriate excitation laser channel (488 nm) to collect at least 30 measurements of 10 s each per sample.
Ensure that the laser intensity and detector alignment remain the same for each sample.
Measure controls including a blank sample without labelled siRNA.
Measure controls including a free siRNA sample with labelled siRNA but no mPEG-b-P(APNBMA).
Analyze the data using FCS-specific software.
Identify the baseline count rate of each sample by determining the stable count rate during a time when no nanocarriers are passing through the confocal volume.
Subtract the count rate of the blank sample from every sample baseline count rate value.
Normalize the resulting values to the free siRNA control to calculate the percent of free siRNA.
Create scripts using a mathematical programming language to predict gene silencing.
Write ordinary differential equations for mRNA production and degradation.
Write ordinary differential equations for siRNA production and degradation.
Write ordinary differential equations for protein production and degradation.
Determine half-lives of mRNA and protein for the gene(s) of interest experimentally or from literature.
Determine doubling time for the cell line.
Input determined values into appropriate degradation rate expressions.
Tune the production rate constants so that gene expression levels remain steady at a normalized value of 100 if no siRNA is introduced.
Set [siRNA] to zero.
Vary kmRNA, ksiRNA, and kprot until [mRNA] and [protein] remain within 1% of the initial normalized value of 100% for the duration of the simulation.
Adjust the initial relative concentration of siRNA in the script based on estimates from gel electrophoresis and FCS assays.
Vary [siRNA] to be proportional to the relative amount of released siRNA, with a value of 100 corresponding to the maximum amount.
Culture NIH/3T3 murine embryonic fibroblasts according to supplier protocols.
Grow cells in growth medium (DMEM supplemented with 10% heat-inactivated fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin-streptomycin).
Maintain cells at 37 °C in a humidified environment with 5% CO2.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Dilute cells in supplemented growth media to a concentration of 75,000 cells/mL.
Add 2 mL of cell suspension (75,000 cells/mL) to each well of the 6-well plate.
Let the cells adhere and recover for 24 h in the incubator.
Wash cells with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Add 1.5 mL of serum- and antibiotic-free transfection medium to each well.
Formulate the siRNA nanocarriers according to steps 1.1-1.2.
Add 25 µL of nanocarrier solution containing 30 pmol of siRNA to each well.
Gently pipette the media up and down to mix.
Place cells in the incubator for 3 h.
Remove transfection media from wells.
Wash each well with PBS.
Add 1 mL of supplemented growth media to each well.
Place cells in the incubator to recover for 30 min.
Remove supplemented growth media from cells.
Add 1 mL of transfection media (without phenol red) to each well.
Calibrate and set a UV laser with a 365 nm filter to an intensity of 200 W/m².
Place cells on a hot plate set to 37 °C.
Remove the plate cover of the cells.
Irradiate cells from above the plate for up to 20 min using the UV laser at an intensity of 200 W m⁻².
Remove transfection media after irradiation.
Add 2 mL of supplemented growth media to each well.
Place cells in incubator until further analysis (e.g., 24 h for qPCR and 48 h for Western blotting).
Measure changes in gene expression using Western blotting.
Measure changes in gene expression using qPCR.
Use fluorescence microscopy to visualize genes with visible signals, such as GFP.
Culture cells according to steps 5.1-5.7.
Prepare a photomask using aluminum foil and black construction paper.
Glue the aluminum foil and construction paper together to form a single unit.
Cut or punch the desired shape into the photomask using a sharp-edged blade or hole-puncher.
Glue the photomask to the bottom of the 6-well plate with the pattern centered under the well containing the cells, ensuring that the anti-reflective side faces the plate.
Set up two ring stands approximately 25 cm apart and attach a platform to each ring stand so that the platforms are of equal height.
Suspend the cell plate between the two stands by resting the plate on top of the platforms.
Ensure that the plate is level.
Irradiate the cells from below the sample for the desired time (up to 20 min) using the UV laser with a 365 nm filter at an intensity of 200 W/m².
Remove the transfection media and add 2 mL of supplemented growth media.
Place in incubator to recover for at least 24 hours.
Image the cells using fluorescence microscopy.
